supported_relationship: Administrative payment infrastructure/activity can be compared with population measures only as separate evidence classes and dates.
not_supported: Infrastructure growth proves population use or inclusion.

supported_relationship: Population use evidence provides demand-side context for administrative payment-system measures.
not_supported: One source can substitute for the other.

supported_relationship: A provider’s authority/listing state is one input to access analysis, but operating location requires separate evidence.
not_supported: Licensed/listed provider equals operating point.

supported_relationship: Verified operating geography can add service-presence context to provider authority records.
not_supported: A location proves the complete set of operating providers.

supported_relationship: Payment regulation, projects and institutions may be upstream mechanisms through which payment capacity changes; each downstream state requires evidence.
not_supported: Reform milestone caused adoption or inclusion.

supported_relationship: Observed payment activity can be placed beside reform milestones to show which downstream states are measured.
not_supported: Temporal sequence alone is causal proof.

supported_relationship: Firm demand and constraint evidence provides context for institutional finance supply and credit evidence.
not_supported: Institutional portfolio growth satisfies firm finance need.

supported_relationship: Institutional lending/portfolio measures and firm-side credit experience may be compared only when units, populations and periods are explicit.
not_supported: Portfolio size equals number of financed firms or welfare.

supported_relationship: Macro and corridor remittance evidence can contextualize household financial behavior while remaining separate from household survey measures.
not_supported: Macro inflows equal household receipt/use rates.

supported_relationship: Household survey receipt/channel behavior can be compared conceptually with remittance flow/cost evidence if periods and bases remain visible.
not_supported: Household percentages can be converted into macro values without a valid bridge.

supported_relationship: MA-001 and MA-003 define measurements that would materially improve current people-side decisions.
not_supported: The gap itself is evidence of deterioration.

supported_relationship: MA-004 defines the missing national firm-finance journey needed to move beyond bounded survey/programme evidence.
not_supported: Existing bounded evidence is invalid.

supported_relationship: MA-005 defines the active access-point register required before a national operating-access atlas is defensible.
not_supported: Blank map areas have zero access.

supported_relationship: MA-002 and MA-010 define active-use and reform-transmission measurements not supplied by infrastructure totals alone.
not_supported: Transactions or terminals equal unique active users.

supported_relationship: MA-006 and MA-010 identify downstream redress/service-quality evidence needed beyond rules and milestones.
not_supported: Missing outcome data means reform failure.

supported_relationship: POS device growth is an administrative infrastructure signal for the Payments page.
not_supported: POS devices are people or active merchants.

supported_relationship: Findex account ownership is a representative people-side measure for its wave and fieldwork period.
not_supported: It is a 2026 population rate.

supported_relationship: The bank roster establishes a source-specific listing/licensing state.
not_supported: The roster establishes current branch operation or market activity.

supported_relationship: The programme KPI is a programme result for MSMEs supported by the Small and Micro Enterprise Promotion Service (SMEPS).
not_supported: It is a national MSME access rate.

supported_relationship: External-sector remittance vintages describe macro flows under the source’s concept.
not_supported: They equal payment-system or informal-channel volumes.

supported_relationship: Comparison depends on two or more evidence records exposing the same compatibility fields.
not_supported: A comparison result can override the source evidence records.

supported_relationship: The chronology provides dated context for conflict shocks, liquidity, FX, import finance, external support and banking conditions around financial intermediation.
not_supported: The chronology proves that a specific macro/policy event caused a financial-inclusion outcome.

supported_relationship: FX availability and import-finance conditions can constrain the environment in which firms trade and seek finance; firm-side effects still require firm evidence.
not_supported: A macro FX/import-finance shock quantifies firm credit access or firm outcomes.

supported_relationship: Remittance flows and revisions can be read alongside FX, reserves and external-balance conditions while preserving source scope and statistical vintage.
not_supported: Macro remittance values equal payment-channel volumes, household receipt rates or informal remittances.

supported_relationship: Currency fragmentation, liquidity and institutional changes provide context for the operating environment of payment rails.
not_supported: A currency or liquidity event proves payment adoption, reach or user outcome.

supported_relationship: Dated policy, support and institutional events can be placed beside reform states to show sequence and system conditions.
not_supported: Temporal ordering proves reform causality or outcome.
